applicant_categories.label: German Abitur (Allgemeine Hochschulreife)
applicant_categories.description: The reference German secondary school-leaving qualification; treated as the direct-entrance standard against which other qualifications are assessed for equivalence.

applicant_categories.label: International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma
applicant_categories.description: Direct entrance if >=24 points, >=3 HL subjects meeting the group 1-4 distribution, and HL Mathematics (Analysis & Approaches or Applications & Interpretation) for technical-field access; SL-only math restricts access away from technical/natural-science/math fields.

applicant_categories.label: British-patterned GCE A-Level
applicant_categories.description: Direct entrance if 3 A-Level subjects at minimum grade C, at least 2 from a defined subject list; natural science studies specifically require 2 A-Levels from mathematics/biology/chemistry/physics/computer science. AS-Levels and GCSEs do not count.

applicant_categories.label: U.S. High School Diploma / AP route
applicant_categories.description: A US high school diploma alone does not grant direct entrance. Direct entrance is possible only via AP examinations taken during high school with results issued directly by the College Board. Otherwise, ZAB assessment typically routes the applicant to Studienkolleg.

applicant_categories.label: EU/EEA or equivalent state (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway)

admission_stages.name: International qualification recognition (uni-assist VPD)
admission_stages.description: Credentials equivalent to the German university entrance qualification (Abitur) grant direct admission eligibility. Subject-restricted qualifications carry the same restriction at TUM. All international applicants must obtain Preliminary Documentation (VPD) from uni-assist, which determines whether the credential grants general or subject-specific admission. Non-comparable qualifications route to Studienkolleg (see the separate preparatory_pathway stage).

criteria.description: Must be equivalent to the German university entrance qualification, or meet subject-restricted admission rules.

admission_stages.name: Eignungsfeststellungsverfahren (Aptitude Assessment, EFV)
admission_stages.description: Two-stage, points-based Aptitude Assessment used for Bachelor Informatik in place of a numerus-clausus lottery/cutoff. Whether internationally-recognized-equivalent qualifications (A-Level, IB) run through an adapted version of this exact point formula, or a different process, is unresolved from official sources (open question, not guessed).

criteria.description: School-leaving diploma average, converted via formula.
Mathematik x3, Deutsch x1, Englisch x1, one natural science subject x2, converted via formula.

Up to 6 bonus points: relevant apprenticeship (>1yr: 6pts), relevant internship (6-12mo: 3pts), MINT studies already completed at TUM (2pts), or Jugend Forscht/Math Olympiad at state level or above (2pts).

criteria.criterion_name: Stage-2 written test (73-83 point band only)
criteria.description: ~90-minute written test, ~20-30 questions, 50% German/50% English; final score 50% HZB average + 50% test result.

admission_stages.name: Studienkolleg preparatory pathway (T-course track)
admission_stages.description: Alternative branch at the qualification-recognition point (not a sequential step after Stage 2): when a qualification is not comparable to German standards, the applicant must complete Studienkolleg (2 semesters, T-course track for Informatics) and pass the Feststellungspruefung before admission eligibility exists at all. A fresh online application plus a new uni-assist VPD is required after completion.

criteria.description: Exit examination; passing grants subject-specific access to the degree program.

extension_metadata.note: sequence_order is set to 1 (same as qualification-recognition) because this is an alternative branch at that decision point, not a step that follows Stage 2 of the aptitude assessment. Studienkolleg students are explicitly exempt from the non-EU tuition fee (see de-tu-munich-cost-eu-eea/non-eu CostProfile records).

source_records.title: Admission Procedures
source_records.excerpt: TUM employs the 'Aptitude Assessment' (Eignungsfeststellungsverfahren) for specific Bachelor's/Master's programs, distinct from unrestricted admission and NC systems. Bachelor's: grade point average and subject-specific grades evaluated using a point system defined per-program. Depending on points: immediate admission, invitation to interview/written test, or rejection. 'no lotteries will be held after final selections have been made.'

source_records.title: International Applicants
source_records.excerpt: An applicant is 'international' when they 'have completed your secondary school education outside of Germany or with something other than a German Abitur.' International students who did not obtain their entrance qualification in the German education system must apply for Preliminary Documentation (VPD) via uni-assist.

source_records.title: Preparatory Study at the Studienkolleg
source_records.excerpt: 'Some international secondary school certificates do not directly qualify students to study at a German university.' Studienkolleg lasts 2 semesters, ending in the Feststellungspruefung, which enables 'subject-specific access to a degree program.' Studienkolleg Muenchen offers G/M/T/W course tracks (T = Technical/Mathematical/Natural Science, relevant to Informatics). German B2 required before admission. From WS2025/26, only one course track per applicant. After completion, a new online application + fresh uni-assist VPD is required.

source_records.title: International Higher Education Entrance Qualification
source_records.excerpt: Applicants whose credentials are 'equivalent to the German university entrance qualification' may gain direct admission. If a qualification permits 'certain subjects only' in the home country, 'subject-bound admission also applies when you enroll as a student at TUM.' When qualifications are not comparable, applicants must complete Studienkolleg and pass the university qualification assessment examination. All international applicants must obtain a VPD from uni-assist, which verifies whether credentials entitle 'general or subject-specific university admission.'

source_records.title: Tuition Fees for Students from Non-EU Countries
source_records.excerpt: Bachelor's programs: 'usually 2,000 or 3,000 euros per semester.' Master's: 'usually 4,000 or 6,000 euros per semester.' 'From the winter semester 2024/25, tuition fees for international students from third countries will only be charged for newly enrolled students in Bachelor's and Master's degree programs.' Exempt: EU/EEA/equivalent-state students; students already enrolled before WS2024/25 in the same program; doctoral/exchange/visiting students; Studienkolleg students; state-examination/non-degree program students.
source_records.notes: Re-fetched independently at a distinct timestamp from the extraction pass; result identical to first fetch -- no discrepancy found. Program-specific tier (2,000 vs 3,000) for Informatics B.Sc. not resolved on this or the program detail page -- see md-01.

source_records.title: Study fees and costs
source_records.excerpt: Cost of living estimates: Munich area 'approximately 1,300 to 2,000 euros (for a single-person household)' monthly. Straubing/Heilbronn 'approximately 900 to 1,200 euros' monthly. 'International students from third countries ... usually have to pay tuition fees.'

source_records.title: Semester fees payment at Munich, Garching, WZW and TUM Asia
source_records.excerpt: 'Currently, the semester fee amounts to 97.00 Euro' -- described as the 'basic contribution for the student union', applicable to students at Munich, Garching, Weihenstephan (WZW), and TUM Asia campuses.

source_records.title: FAQs regarding the Studierendenwerk Fee
source_records.source_organization: Studierendenwerk Muenchen Oberbayern (public-law student services institution)
source_records.excerpt: 'Current Amount: EUR 97 per semester (increased from EUR 85)', 'Effective Date: from the 2026 Summer Semester onwards'. Funds subsidized canteen meals, childcare, free advisory/counselling (social, BAfoeG, legal, coaching), student housing support. Does NOT include a public transport ticket -- a separate 'Semesterticket/Ermaessigungsticket' exists independently.

source_records.title: Language Certificates
source_records.excerpt: 'A list of certificates recognized as proof of German language proficiency can be found in the KMK framework regulations' (external PDF). 'Applicants holding a German university entrance qualification do not require verification of their German language skills.' 'German citizens with an international higher education entrance qualification who have spent at least two school years at a German school may submit two annual school certificates.' No mention of a separate English-language proficiency requirement for German-taught programs anywhere on this page.

source_records.title: Recognition of the General Certificate of Education (GCE) in Germany
source_records.excerpt: 'you must provide evidence of 3 general, independent subjects at A Level with a minimum grade of C.' At least 2 of the 3 from a defined list (language, history, geography, social studies/politics, economics, mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, computer science). 'Natural science studies' requires '2 A Level from: mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, computer science.' GCSEs 'CANNOT be taken into consideration for access to higher education institutions in Germany.'
source_records.notes: Re-fetched independently at a distinct timestamp; result identical to first fetch.

source_records.title: uni-assist Country Information: United Kingdom
source_records.excerpt: 'Predicted grades issued by your school are not sufficient for a university application in Germany.' 'Please always submit all of your A Levels because we can only determine which A Levels can be taken into consideration for a specific application once we have completed our evaluation.' 'AS Levels cannot be taken into consideration.' Directs applicants to anabin.kmk.org for detailed equivalency. uni-assist is the official document pre-screening body TUM directs applicants to for VPD issuance.

source_records.title: uni-assist Country Information: United States
source_records.excerpt: 'A US high school diploma alone does not allow you to study in Germany.' Credentials assessed via ZAB (Central Office for Foreign Education) standards; typically qualifies for Studienkolleg. Direct admission possible ONLY through AP examinations: 'AP examinations can only be taken into consideration, if the examination was taken during your time at high school' and 'AP results must be issued by the College Board. Results issued by the High School are not sufficient.' Required: high school diploma with grade 9-12 subject/grade overview and unweighted CGPA.

source_records.title: Recognition of the IB-Diploma in Germany
source_records.excerpt: Minimum '24 points ... achieved from the six examination subjects'. 'At least three subjects must be completed at the Higher Level (HL)' (alternatively four). Required: two languages (group 1/2), a social science subject (group 3), a natural science subject -- Biology/Chemistry/Physics (group 4). Mathematics rule (from 2021): HL 'Analysis and Approaches' or 'Applications and Interpretation' -> 'direct university admission for all subjects.' SL Mathematics only -> access restricted to 'subjects that are not assigned to the mathematics, natural sciences and technical fields' (Informatics is a technical field). Exception: schools on the official IB-Diploma Recognition Agreement list may qualify for general access despite SL math if other requirements are met.
source_records.notes: Re-fetched independently at a distinct timestamp; result identical to first fetch -- the HL-math-for-technical-fields rule is confirmed consistent both times.

source_records.title: Uebersicht EFV B.Sc. Informatik inkl. Berechnungsbeispiel
source_records.source_organization: TUM School of Computation, Information and Technology (CIT)
source_records.retrieval_method: WebFetch PDF text extraction (independent re-fetch, second pass)
source_records.excerpt: Stage 1 (100-point scale): 65% HZB (school-leaving diploma) average via formula 120-20x(grade); 35% best individual subject grades (Mathematik 3x, Deutsch 1x, Englisch 1x, natural science [Physics/Chemistry/Biology/Informatik, all 4 semesters] 2x) via formula 10+6x(average); up to 6 bonus points (relevant apprenticeship >1yr: 6; relevant internship 6-12mo: 3; MINT studies at TUM: 2; Jugend Forscht/Math Olympiad state+: 2). Thresholds: '84 Punkte und mehr = direkte Zulassung'; '73-83 Punkte = Einladung zum Test (Stufe 2)'; '72 Punkte und weniger = Ablehnung'. Stage 2 (50% HZB average + 50% test result, ~90min, ~20-30 questions, 50% German/50% English, math/logic/interdisciplinary problem-solving): '70 Punkte und mehr = Eignung festgestellt = Zulassung'; '69 Punkte und weniger = keine Eignung = Absage'.
source_records.notes: Re-fetched independently at a distinct timestamp; all thresholds and weightings identical on both passes -- no discrepancy. This is the run's single most material extension_metadata fact block.

source_records.source_organization: TUM School of Computation, Information and Technology (CIT)

Semester koennen Sie individuelle Schwerpunkte setzen.' Application: '15. Mai bis 15. Juli' online via TUMonline for Winter Semester; Stage 2 test date 'Freitag, 21.08.2026' (confirming this is the Winter Semester 2026/27 admissions cycle, the current published cycle). Required documents: diploma, CV, ID, language certificates where applicable, uni-assist pre-screening for international applicants. Students select one 'Anwendungsfach' (application field): Elektrotechnik, Maschinenwesen, Mathematik, Medizin, or Wirtschaftswissenschaften; custom fields possible with examination-board approval.

source_records.title: The Deutschlandstipendium at TUM

Funding: matched, 'the federal government helps out too' -- private-donor contributions are doubled by federal government pledges (2026 Matching Challenge). Selection: 'It's not just your grades that count, but also your personal achievements' -- academic performance, personal responsibility/commitment, individual life circumstances. source_records.title: Deutschlandstipendium -- Application and being sponsored
source_records.excerpt: 'Both Bachelor's and Master's students at TUM, as well as high school graduates who would like to begin their studies at TUM in the coming semester, can apply' -- confirms first-year/incoming applicants are eligible, not only continuing students. 'The next application period for the 2027/28 funding year will take place in the summer of 2027' -- exact dates announced spring 2027 (not yet published). 'The duration of the scholarship is based on your standard period of study.' Renewal requires minimum grade and ECTS thresholds annually, with documented exceptions for illness/caregiving/childcare; otherwise students reapply as new applicants.

source_records.source_organization: Federal Foreign Office of Germany (Auswaertiges Amt)
source_records.excerpt: 'The amount to be paid into the account varies depending on the purpose of your stay and is based on the maximum rates for support received by German students' (i.e., tied to BAfoeG maximum support/Bedarfssatz rates, not a fixed university-set figure). Applicants directed to 'the website of the competent mission abroad or in the Consular Services Portal' for the exact current amount -- no numeric figure is published on this specific official page.

source_records.title: Germany: Blocked bank accounts for students (Guide)
source_records.excerpt: 'The required amount for a German blocked account when applying for a student visa in 2026 is EUR 11,904 ... with a monthly withdrawal limit set at EUR 992.' States this is based on BAfoeG-defined estimated annual living expenses, consistent with the mechanism confirmed by src-19, but does not itself cite or link an official Auswaertiges Amt publication.
source_records.notes: NOT treated as authoritative evidence per this project's source hierarchy (secondary/commercial site). Used only as a corroborating, non-authoritative candidate figure alongside a second independent secondary source (germany-visa.org) that reported the identical EUR 11,904 / EUR 992 figures. The exact number could not be confirmed on an official government page despite multiple fetch attempts -- see missing-data.json md-04.

source_records.title: Rahmenordnung ueber Deutsche Sprachpruefungen fuer das Studium an deutschen Hochschulen (RO-DT)
source_records.excerpt: The KMK framework regulations document that TUM's Language Certificates page (src-10) directly links to as 'a list of certificates recognized as proof of German language proficiency'. Recognized routes to unrestricted admission: DSH-2 (Deutsche Sprachpruefung fuer den Hochschulzugang, level 2 minimum); TestDaF at TDN 4 minimum across all four modules; the German-language component of a Studienkolleg Feststellungspruefung. Exempting qualifications (no additional test required): Goethe-Zertifikat C2 (Grosses Deutsches Sprachdiplom), OeSD C2 (Oesterreichisches Sprachdiplom C2), telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule, DSD II (Deutsches Sprachdiplom der Kultusministerkonferenz, level II).
source_records.notes: Hosted on TUM's own domain and directly cited by TUM's official Language Certificates page (src-10) as the authoritative certificate list; treated as official_university tier given that direct institutional endorsement, even though the regulation itself is a KMK (state-level) instrument.

source_records.title: Satzung zur Aenderung der Hochschulgebuehren- und Entgeltsatzung der TUM (2024-012, 12.02.2024)
source_records.retrieval_method: WebFetch PDF text extraction (independent re-fetch, second pass)
source_records.excerpt: Official TUM statute (Satzung) governing university fees and charges, effective 2023-10-01. The fee-schedule annex assigns each Bachelor's/Master's program to a numbered fee tier for non-EU/third-country-national students. Exact row: 'Bachelor CIT Informatik, B.Sc. 2 3.000 €' -- i.e. TUM School of Computation, Information and Technology's Bachelor Informatik is assigned fee tier 2, which corresponds to 3,000 EUR per semester (6,000 EUR/year), resolving the 2,000-vs-3,000 EUR/semester ambiguity left open in src-01/src-06.
source_records.notes: Re-fetched independently at a distinct timestamp within the same research session; the table row was identical on both passes -- no discrepancy. A binding institutional statute, ranked as an official_university primary source per this project's source hierarchy -- stronger evidence than the general (non-program-specific) tuition overview page.
